tips: Leave your phone face-down and locked to find Pokémon. Checking the time on the lock screen is fine; only unlocking resets the counter.
Up to nine Pokémon can wait on your Glyph Matrix. The rarest one is always shown first.
The longer your phone stays locked, the rarer the Pokémon: uncommon ones peak after an hour, rare ones after an hour and a half.
Very rare Pokémon, like Dratini, Gible or starters from other regions, become most likely after two hours without unlocking.
Pokémon keep appearing quietly while you sleep. Sleep six hours without unlocking and you'll be well rested: rarer Pokémon all the next day.
Each fishing rod hooks different aquatic Pokémon. Only one rod can be active at a time, so pick the one for the Pokémon you're after.
One in 512 wild Pokémon is shiny. On the Glyph Matrix it shows as a negative image and flashes longer when it appears.
Shinies are twice as common during the Halloween and Christmas weeks, and four times as common on the big days.
Turn on the Everstone in a Pokémon's details to stop it from evolving when it levels up.
Tyrogue and Clamperl let you choose what they evolve into. Wurmple and Burmy decide for themselves.
Castform changes with the weather, and Deerling with the season. Collect them all!
There are 28 Unown to find: every letter, plus ! and ?
Check the Rumors page in the Pokédex. New rumors about legendary Pokémon unlock as your Pokédex grows, as long as you have that region's Pokédex.
Complete missions to earn items and a boost that makes rarer Pokémon appear for a while.
Export your progress from Settings to keep a backup, or to move it to another phone.
Halloween brings Ghost-type Pokémon all day long. Evolved forms may appear after dark…
Rainy days attract Water-types and Grass-types, and storms bring out Electric-types.
When your battery runs low, certain Electric-type Pokémon may appear. Keep an eye out below 10%.
Some Pokémon are only active at night. Watch out for Zubat and Hoothoot after dark!
The full moon awakens Fairy-type Pokémon. Clefairy loves to dance under moonlight!
Ancient Pokémon restored from fossils appear as your Pokédex progresses.
Train the same partner for several days in a row: some Pokémon only respect dedicated trainers.
Catching a Pokémon you already have gives you a Rare Candy. The Repel skips them if you only want new ones.
On Valentine's Day, Pokémon Day, New Year and San Juan, special Pokémon gather. Keep an eye on the calendar!
Whenever you catch a Pokémon, you might just find a new item in your bag.
Baby Pokémon like Pichu or Togepi only hatch from Eggs. You'll find your first ones once you have the Johto Pokédex. You can carry three at once, and they hatch while your phone stays locked.
Each professor gives you their region's Pokédex as yours grows: Johto at 50 Pokémon, Hoenn at 120, Sinnoh at 200 and Unova at 300.
Tap the phone at the top of the Home screen to open the Pokégear. A red dot means a professor has something for you; otherwise, they'll tell you how your Pokédex is going and the latest rumors.
Some legendary Pokémon won't appear without their key item, like the Eon Ticket. When you hear their rumor, their professor will have it waiting on the Pokégear.
A released legendary Pokémon can appear again, one at a time. Good news for shiny hunters: a legendary is shiny 1 in 32 times.
With all four regional Pokédexes, Professor Oak gives you the Town Map to choose which regions' Pokémon appear.
Complete the national Pokédex and Professor Oak will reward you with the Shiny Charm.
Leaving your phone to charge? Electric-type Pokémon like Pikachu, Magnemite or Shinx gather around it.
Long-press your home screen to add the Glyph Catch widgets: your team, or the Pokémon waiting on your Glyph Matrix. Pick their backgrounds in Settings → Appearance.
Add up to six favorites to your team from each Pokémon's details. With the Exp. Share, Professor Oak's gift when you reach Unova, the whole team earns experience.
Some PC Box wallpapers are locked: each one is an achievement, like catching a Pikachu or hatching 10 Eggs. Find them in Settings → Appearance.
With no wild Pokémon around, your Glyph Matrix can show a companion instead of the clock. Choose it with "Show on the Glyph Matrix" in its details.
Every catch of a species adds to its shiny chain: at 10, 25 and 50 catches its shiny becomes more likely. Each Pokémon's details show how far you are.
Too many Pidgey? In the PC, the Repeated filter shows only species you have more than once, and "All but one" picks them for release while keeping one of each.
A Bug Catcher gives you Honey soon after the Sinnoh Pokédex. Spread it from your Bag and Pokémon with a sweet tooth, like Combee or Heracross, come for an hour.
Light an Incense and Pokémon appear twice as fast for an hour. You can win them in missions or find one now and then when you catch a Pokémon.
At 150 species, the clerk brings you the Super Repel: only Pokémon you don't have in your PC come close. Legendaries are never scared off by a repel.
Keep your favorites in your team and train them. With lots of friendship they train harder for you, and some species only evolve thanks to it.
